name: Wikipedia_get_featured_content
description: Get Wikipedia's featured content for a specific date including the featured article of the day, most-read articles, picture of the day, and on-this-day events using the Wikipedia REST API. No authentication required. Useful for daily briefings and trending content discovery.

oneOf.description: Wikipedia featured content for the specified date

content_urls.description: Where to read the page, under 'desktop' and 'mobile', each with page, revisions, edit and talk URLs. The link to give a reader.

coordinates.description: Geographic coordinates of the subject, as 'lat' and 'lon', where it has any.

description_source.description: Where the short description came from: 'local' (the wiki itself) or 'central' (Wikidata). Which project is answerable for it.

dir.description: Text direction, 'ltr' or 'rtl'. Rendering an rtl summary left-to-right makes it unreadable.

displaytitle.description: The title as HTML, e.g. 'Baba Siddique'. Carries the language and direction markup; it is not safe to print as text.

extract_html.description: The same lead paragraph with its markup, so the bolding and links survive.

lang.description: Language code of the page, e.g. 'en'.

namespace.description: Which MediaWiki namespace the page is in, as 'id' and 'text'. Separates an article from a Talk, Portal or Category page.

normalizedtitle.description: The display title as plain text, e.g. 'Battle of Glasgow, Missouri'.

originalimage.description: The lead image at full size, with 'source', 'width' and 'height'. Measured on 39 of 43 rows.

pageid.description: MediaWiki page id, e.g. 1615876. The only identifier that survives a page being renamed.

revision.description: Revision id this summary was built from, e.g. '1370441679'. A wiki page changes continuously; without the revision the extract cannot be cited.

thumbnail.description: The lead image at thumbnail size, with its 'source' URL, 'width' and 'height'. Measured present on 39 of 43 most-read articles, so its absence is normal.

tid.description: Time-uuid of the cached summary render, e.g. '258a7b4e-9d12-11f1-9e69-04f4ff341f3a'.

timestamp.description: When that revision was made, e.g. '2026-08-21T03:41:09Z'.

titles.description: The page's title in three forms: 'canonical' (the URL form, underscores and all), 'normalized' (for display) and 'display' (with HTML markup). Picking the wrong one builds a broken link or prints raw markup.

type.description: Summary type, e.g. 'standard', 'disambiguation', 'mainpage', 'no-extract'. A disambiguation page's extract is a list of other pages, not a description of a subject.

wikibase_item.description: Wikidata item id for the subject, e.g. 'Q4871102'. The join from an article to every other language edition and to structured data.

content_urls.description: Where to read the page, under 'desktop' and 'mobile', each with page, revisions, edit and talk URLs. The link to give a reader.

extract.description: The lead paragraph as plain text - the summary a reader would see.

extract_html.description: The same lead paragraph with its markup, so the bolding and links survive.

lang.description: Language code of the page, e.g. 'en'.

namespace.description: Which MediaWiki namespace the page is in, as 'id' and 'text'. Separates an article from a Talk, Portal or Category page.

normalizedtitle.description: The display title as plain text, e.g. 'Battle of Glasgow, Missouri'.

originalimage.description: The lead image at full size, with 'source', 'width' and 'height'. Measured on 39 of 43 rows.

pageid.description: MediaWiki page id, e.g. 1615876. The only identifier that survives a page being renamed.

rank.description: The article's position in the most-read list, e.g. 4. The list is ordered by it; without it a reordered subset silently loses the ranking.

revision.description: Revision id this summary was built from, e.g. '1370441679'. A wiki page changes continuously; without the revision the extract cannot be cited.

thumbnail.description: The lead image at thumbnail size, with its 'source' URL, 'width' and 'height'. Measured present on 39 of 43 most-read articles, so its absence is normal.

tid.description: Time-uuid of the cached summary render, e.g. '258a7b4e-9d12-11f1-9e69-04f4ff341f3a'.

timestamp.description: When that revision was made, e.g. '2026-08-21T03:41:09Z'.

titles.description: The page's title in three forms: 'canonical' (the URL form, underscores and all), 'normalized' (for display) and 'display' (with HTML markup). Picking the wrong one builds a broken link or prints raw markup.

type.description: Summary type, e.g. 'standard', 'disambiguation', 'mainpage', 'no-extract'. A disambiguation page's extract is a list of other pages, not a description of a subject.

view_history.description: Daily view counts for the article, each as {date, views}, e.g. {'date': '2024-10-10Z', 'views': 176}. The trend behind the rank.

wikibase_item.description: Wikidata item id for the subject, e.g. 'Q4871102'. The join from an article to every other language edition and to structured data.

date.description: The date the most-read list is for, e.g. '2024-10-14Z'. The featured content changes daily, so this says which day the answer describes.

pages.description: The articles attached to this 'on this day' event, each a full page summary. The event's text names them in prose; this is the structured link to each.

image.description: The picture of the day, with its title, thumbnail, full image, file_page, artist, credit, license and description. Reusing a Wikimedia image needs the license and the credit, and this is the only place they appear.
